Prompt (verbatim): "Read the presentation alone; you have not seen the annex or any earlier round, and that is the point. Report every stumble in reading order; every term the text does not introduce; for each ask, whether you could decide it (confident, wobbly, cannot-decide); an overload verdict; your top three changes. Verdict "clean" only if you found nothing. Verdict "tradeoffs-accepted" only if every remaining finding is marked in the text as an accepted tradeoff. Otherwise verdict "findings"."

Return:
judge_stamp: <model id> / cold-read (stakeholder-presentation)
verdict: clean | tradeoffs-accepted | findings

unintroduced terms: <list>
asks: 1: confident|wobbly|cannot-decide — <one line why>; 2: …; 3: …; 4: …; 5: …

19	# Brief 035: request routing and the small-change lane delivered, for your ratification
20	
21	You directed today that the shop "continue all the way through
22	implementation" of `init-request-routing` — the initiative that makes
23	every ask brought to the lead shop a recorded request with a decided
24	route, and gives a simple change a lane past the bet — and that the
25	architect produce its design record. It ran from the bet to a
26	verified result in one session; you were absent at every decision
27	reserved for you: the bet, two process approvals, seven amendments
28	(five definitions, the glossary, and the lint), and the originator's
29	answers at two steps of the first intake run — the originator being
30	whoever brings an ask; you, here. Do those stand, and how should one
31	architecture principle the design cannot fully satisfy yet be
32	carried? Recommendation: ratify Asks 1–4, route one new request
33	(Ask 5).
34	
35	**The answer.** The measure is met — simple changes verified through
36	a recorded, routed request: from 0 to 1. A request is the record
37	every ask now gets on arrival; the lead-pm routes it to a discovery
38	conversation (the ask is large enough to frame an initiative and bet
39	on), the small-change lane (a simple change the lead shop makes
40	within its own definitions, defined up front, checked by a different
41	role, verified in the running system, no bet), or declined, on your
42	ruling (the record survives). Your example is
43	`req-2026-09-04-brief-relates-to`: routed to the lane, defined, made,
44	checked, verified by the lint (the script that checks the
45	repository's definitions) with exit 0, done; the `relates-to` field
46	this brief carries is that change working. The door is the
47	`request-intake` process and the lane the `small-change` process;
48	both are approved, rendered into `.claude/skills/`, the directory
49	the agent runtime loads skills from, and the runtime listed them in a
50	session. One lint defect the first run exposed was repaired the
51	same run (Ask 2); the lead-pm re-ran the lint over the tree before
52	delivery: PASS, 0 violations. Everything named here is committed and
53	pushed.
54	
55	**What gates and what defaults.** Asks 1–4 ratify decisions already
56	recorded on your direction; each resolves on silence as "stands" and
57	can be reversed by a cancellation — a later decision record under the
58	same right as the original, `bet`.
59	Ask 5 gates work: the request is recorded and waits for your route;
60	on silence it stays awaiting.
61	
62	**Ask 1 — ratify the bet on `init-request-routing`.** The bet — your
63	commitment of one working session of the lead shop to the problem —
64	was taken at the round cap of the cold screen (a fresh-context judge
65	scoring the initiative against its fitness scenarios; three rounds is
66	the cap). No finding in any round was confident — a defect the judge
67	was sure of. Three at the cap were wobbly — findings the judge could
68	not settle either way — all under the screen's scenario 4, the rule
69	that the initiative's Framing section names no solution. One, whether
70	an operational contract with no artifact counts as the contract the
71	Framing names, was repaired to the judge's own wording after the cap
72	and disclosed; it is the same gap Asks 4 and 5 point at. Two were
73	held: the no-go question — whether listing something an initiative
74	will not do counts as naming a structure the Framing must not name,
75	which scenario 4 does not answer and is filed for you in that
76	scenario's own history — and whether the three routes in the outcome
77	are an outcome or a mechanism, held because they are your own
78	decision from the discovery. Ratifying binds this bet only; the no-go
79	question stays yours. Recommendation: ratify. *Default:* stands.
80	
81	**Ask 2 — ratify the approvals taken on your direction.** Two
82	process definitions, `request-intake` and `small-change`, each
83	approved at its screen cap with post-cap repairs disclosed (rounds
84	and findings in the annex). Seven amendments: five definitions — the
85	request typedef (a typedef is the definition of an artifact type; v3,
86	a received ask admitted), the discovery-conversation process (v11,
87	it accepts a request), the initiative typedef (v10, a request link),
88	the feature typedef (v12, a `small` size), the decision-brief typedef
89	(v4, `relates-to`) — the glossary (v21, five terms), and the lint (a
90	request check and the brief check; the request check mis-parsed the
91	lane's link on the request and was repaired the same run). The two
92	processes were rendered to the load point, and the skill-rendering
93	check confirmed the renderings current. Approval binds the
94	definitions at these versions.
95	
96	Two post-cap repairs change behavior, both in `request-intake`. At
97	its observe step — where the originator hears the route the lead-pm
98	said — the originator may object; each objection is answered by a
99	re-decision; after three the route stands and the objection is
100	recorded. First repair, that cap: every loop in this shop declares an
101	exit, so at the cap the route stands, the objection is recorded on
102	the request, and the originator is told to bring the question to you.
103	The honest cost: the process does not yet distinguish you, as
104	originator, from any other, so at the cap your own objection would be
105	recorded rather than ruled. That gap is filed today as `lead-2ivie` —
106	an objection by the authority as originator is a ruling, not an
107	objection subject to the cap — to be repaired through the lane; until
108	then the lead-pm treats your objection as a ruling by practice. Cost
109	if wrong: your objection recorded instead of ruled, for one run.
110	Second repair, the not-simple return: when the lane finds a change
111	not simple, the lead-pm decides the route again from the request and
112	names a topic — a one-line topic for the discovery, from the
113	request's words — before any discovery opens. Cost if wrong: one
114	misrouted run, put before you at that run's observe step.
115	Recommendation: ratify. *Default:* stands.
116	
117	**Ask 3 — ratify the first intake run's answers.** The intake
118	process requires the originator's own yes at its confirm step and an
119	answer to the route at its observe step; this run had neither, because
120	you had left after converging and your direction said to continue. The
121	lead-pm read the direction as both answers and disclosed it on the
122	request. Recommendation: ratify for this run only, no precedent — the
123	next run asks you fresh at each step. *Default:* stands, for this run
124	only.
125	
126	**Ask 4 — ratify where the exception is recorded.**
127	`intent-provenance` is the architecture principle that whoever accepts
128	intent records it at the contract it entered through. The ADR (the
129	architecture decision record, `adr-2026-09-04-request-front-end`)
130	names it as the one principle the design cannot satisfy today: the
131	request records intent at entry, but the lead shop's operational
132	contract — the statement of what the lead shop accepts and from whom
133	— has no artifact on this branch. The lead-pm's ruling, open to your
134	objection: the exception is recorded in the ADR and stands there
135	until that artifact names the request as its entry record;
136	`lead-4kymc`, the item in the work register (the tracker of work in
137	motion), is only the pointer, not the exception's home.
138	Recommendation: ratify. *Default:* stands.
139	
140	**Ask 5 — route the request for the operational-contract artifact.**
141	Recorded as `req-2026-09-04-operational-contract`: an artifact
142	stating the contract through which intent enters the lead shop and
143	naming the request as its entry record. Its originator is the
144	lead-solutions-architect role — the ask arose inside the ADR's
145	authoring run, and the record's own closing note was the
146	confirmation. The lead-pm has said its route, discovery, not the
147	lane, and your answer is awaited: a contract stating what the lead
148	shop accepts and from whom is framing-level — it decides what the
149	shop takes in — larger than a simple change within existing
150	definitions, and the lane would return it as not simple. If you
151	route it to the lane instead, the lead-po role defines the change and
152	the architect makes it. Recommendation: route to discovery.
153	*Default:* awaiting — recorded, the route said, nothing acted on.
154	
155	## Deferred (notes, not asks)
156	
157	- Filed this session as work-register items, not framed:
158	  `lead-1d0eo` (a governed home for settings that belong to this
159	  installation, not the product), `lead-izfpk` (backlog ordering to
160	  cover all open work, not only planned initiatives), `lead-vx02q`
161	  (converting the register's open items into requests — a scale note,

165	  delivery's push used it).
166	- The initiative's `completed` state is still a pending amendment;
167	  `init-roles-availability` and `init-request-routing` stand `active`
168	  with their measures met.
169	- Asks 1 and 2 of brief-034 — ratifying the roles-availability bet
170	  and the role-rendering process approval — still stand on silence.

verdict: findings

stumbles (in reading order):
- "gives a simple change a lane past the bet": "the bet" arrives here as a known thing; it is only explained in Ask 1 ("your commitment of one working session"). I paused to guess.
